add.issue.name: xlint: check final newline in .md files

edit.description.md:
## Problem

`check_final_newline` runs only in the `.py` branch of `check_file` in `tools/xlint/xlint.py`. A `.md` file gets exactly one check (space indentation), so a missing final newline in Markdown is invisible to xlint.

Hit live 2026-09-27: an edit silently dropped the trailing newline from `.agents/agent-notes-secretary-3.md`. Three sibling notes files all end with a newline, so it was a regression rather than house style — and xlint reported the file clean.

## Scope

- Apply `check_final_newline` to the `.md` branch, under the existing `--no-final-newline` flag.
- Respect the existing fence/frontmatter exemptions where relevant.

## Acceptance

- A `.md` missing its trailing newline fails; one with it passes.
- `--no-final-newline` disables the check for `.md` as it does for `.py`.
- Repo-wide `xlint $(git ls-files '*.md')` is clean, or every remaining finding is dispositioned.

## Notes

- **ai-ok**: an AI may pick this up and implement it without extensive discussion with the human.
- Related: GBNEWPS (frontmatter + fenced-code exemptions) is already implemented in `ed3d27e` but still sits in Todo — that ticket's status looks stale.
- Adjacent, deliberately *not* in scope: `check_trailing_whitespace` is also language-independent and is `.py`-only today. Worth its own ticket.

add.issue.name: Replace the broken coding subagent (mimo) — evaluate nemotron-3-ultra vs north-mini-code for quality

edit.description.md:
`opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` — the model AGENTS.md assigns to coding via `dispatch coding` — **fails instantly** with an opaque `UnknownError` ("Unexpected server error", ref `err_87964db6`, `err_0ac8beb6`). Tried twice on 2026-09-27, not transient; the process never starts. Coding work had to be run on `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` instead, which worked 3/3.

**The evaluation, per the human (2026-09-27):** compare quality of
- `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` — in effect **very cheap**: generous limits, *not*
  bundled into the same pool as big-pickle (unlike mimo and some others), and not
  in the OpenRouter free pool either. So mimo was effectively a *third* generous pool.
- `openrouter/cohere/north-mini-code:free` — a coding specialist (30B MoE, 3B active,
  256K ctx, quality 24). Currently referenced in 5 agent files: `mechanic.md`,
  `programmer.md`, `overseer.md`, `worker-mimo.md`, `worker-north-mini-code.md`.

**Cost asymmetry to weigh:** north-mini-code sits on the **shared OpenRouter `:free`
pool**, which AGENTS.md says to reserve for models with no console equivalent. When
that daily pool hits zero every `:free` model returns empty and everything looks
broken. nemotron-ultra is on opencode's console gateway with generous limits. So
north-mini-code is not merely pricier in tokens — it is on a failure-prone pool.

**The deciding question is quality, because cheapness wins ties.** Cheapness per run
does not compensate for errors, so: given no meaningful change in quality, a cheaper
model is better. That makes this a quality comparison first and a cost comparison
second, with the pool-reliability difference as the tiebreak.

**Method note:** a real quality comparison needs a task with a known-correct answer
and scored output, not a vibe check. The cursor-reviewer-skill trials in
`/storage/cursor-review-baseline/` are the existing precedent for a scored,
frozen-subject comparison — reuse that shape rather than inventing one.

Also settle `programmer.md`'s model pin (see `WV26JZ2`, `3RVME3H`): it names
`worker-north-mini-code` while AGENTS.md's dispatch table says `worker-mimo`, and
the programmer is supposed to delegate coding to a worker anyway.

add.issue.name: Spec: wide all-tasks priority view (separate tool, reuses taskview's selection layer)

edit.description.md:
Write the spec for the **wide / all-tasks priority view** — a separate tool from the tmux pane. Do NOT build it yet; this ticket is for the spec only, and the spec must go through the normal process (AI-written and labelled, or human-written, per the authorship rule in `doc/development.md`).

**Why it is separate** (human, 2026-09-27): dealing with all tasks at once requires a wider perspective than the current taskview provides, whereas the pane is good for focus. Two renderers, one selection layer. Recorded as Decision 13 in `tools/taskview/SPEC.md`.

**Already built for it — do not rebuild:** `tools/taskview/SPEC.md` R21 requires the
selection and metrics logic to be exposed as pure functions over (state, filter) with no
I/O, precisely so this tool can import them rather than reimplement the rules:
`read_csv`, `select_tasks`, `compute_metrics`. The invariant R25 defines
(`shown + filtered_total` = open tasks not never-showed) is the arithmetic any second
renderer must preserve.

**Likely shape to evaluate in the spec:**
- Reads the same CSV — which is the single authority; the epiq boards, `TASKS.md` and
  `STATUS.md` are all derivatives of it, so this tool does not introduce a fourth source.
- Renders a sortable/editable table rather than a fixed condensed pane, so overall
  priority across *all* projects is visible at once.
- Needs an **unfiltered** view, which is what `/storage/Agents/.taskview.yaml` already
  provides for the pane (`categories: []`, `include_bucket: true`).
- The open question this spec must answer: how much does editing belong in it? The human
  floated "possibly even an editable table to manage the overall priority of all tasks",
  which raises the write path — priority is not currently a CSV field, so this may need a
  schema change (a `priority` column) rather than reusing `importance`. That is a real
  decision, not an implementation detail, and it interacts with the append-only
  last-write-wins model.
- Follow `task-windows` (`/storage/Agents/plans/pending/task-windows.md`) as a possible
  consumer: a task window's pane should show only that project, which depends on this
  work having a clean shared selection layer.

**Context:** the project-specific work this depends on is implemented, gated and
uncommitted as of 2026-09-27 — see `doc/reviews/taskview-2026-09-27-a9ee0a.md`.

add.issue.name: Off-vocabulary categories in tasks.csv: research / ai-docs / personal (#61–#63, #65, #66)

edit.description.md:
Five open tasks carry category values that were never ruled on. All five appeared on 2026-09-27, all from the model-benchmark / codebase-comprehension work, and they are the only rows in the entire store that use them.

| # | category | task |
|---|----------|------|
| 61 | `research` | Model benchmark: widen the episode set |
| 62 | `ai-docs` | Correct library/ai/free-model-tier-list.md |
| 63 | `research` | Model benchmark: set G2–G5 thresholds |
| 65 | `personal` | Codebase comprehension learning process |
| 66 | `personal` | First 45-min comprehension block on mms-frontend |

## Why this needs a ruling, not a cleanup

The category column is the membership axis for project-scoped views (SPEC R4, Decision 8). A category only earns its place if some `.taskview.yaml` can scope to it or a pane can ask for it. `research` and `ai-docs` are neither a project nor a life area — they are *activities*. They name what the task is being done for, not what it is about, and that distinction is exactly what the human's rule turns on: **category = what the work is about, not which repo you are sitting in** (SPEC Decision 17).

The deeper problem is accretion. Nothing rejects a new category value, so the vocabulary grows one task at a time, by whoever happens to be in a session. A column that widens silently stops being a vocabulary. It is the same free-text drift already recorded for tags (`verif` vs `verify`), one level up and slower to notice.

## The specific questions

**#61, #62, #63 — model benchmark.** Three defensible answers, genuinely different:

- `work` — `TASKS.md` files the model benchmark under `### Work`.
- `XLib` — the harness lives at `$XLIB/tools/modelbench/`. Precedent: #56 (taskview project-specific) was labelled `XLib` even though its plan lives in the Agents repo, for exactly this reason.
- `Agents` — the plan is `Agents/plans/model-benchmark.md`, the output is `Agents/library/ai/models/`.

`#56` already set the precedent, so `XLib` is the consistent answer unless the human rules the benchmark is work rather than tooling.

**#65, #66 — codebase comprehension.** Almost certainly the same thing as `Personal Development`, spelled differently — `personal` vs `Personal Development` is the `verif`/`verify` drift again. `Personal Development` is the `TASKS.md` section name and is what #22, #23 and #41 were just labelled with in the 2026-09-27 pass, so these two are the odd ones out.

## Left unchanged on purpose

A live session owns this work. Relabelling under it would be invisible to whoever is mid-task and would make the pane disagree with the plan they are reading. Needs the human's ruling first, then one `taskupdate.py update <id> --category ...` per task.

add.issue.name: /storage/Agents/.taskview.yaml documents three categories that do not exist and omits three that do

edit.description.md:
`/storage/Agents/.taskview.yaml` is the file a future agent reads to learn the category vocabulary. Its comment block currently describes a vocabulary that does not match the data, in both directions.

It says:

> In use but not yet ruled on: XLib, Agents, mms-frontend, Mistlands, MaFE.

After the 2026-09-27 labelling pass:

- `mms-frontend`, `Mistlands`, `MaFE` are in **zero** rows. They never have been in any row.
- `XLib` and `Agents` are in use and correctly listed.
- The three values that *are* in use — `research`, `ai-docs`, `personal` — are not mentioned at all (see the sibling ticket on off-vocabulary categories).

So the list names two real values, three fictional ones, and omits three real ones.

## Why it matters more than it looks

This file is the unfiltered global view's own config, and it is the only place the vocabulary is written down anywhere. A filter file that documents categories which do not exist is worse than one that documents none: an agent reading it to answer "what are the valid categories?" gets a confident wrong answer, and `Mistlands` / `MaFE` read as though someone had already ruled those to be projects.

The real vocabulary after 2026-09-27 is nine values: `work`, `XLib`, `Traveller`, `Agents`, `Maintenance`, `Personal Development`, `Business / Career`, `Hobby`, plus `research` / `ai-docs` / `personal` pending the sibling ticket. Of those, only `XLib` has a project filter file today; `Agents` holds the unfiltered one.

## Scope

Rewriting the comment block only — no YAML key changes, and no behaviour change. The human has asked for the file itself to be left alone for now. Not covered by `E5MH4S2` (the wide all-tasks view), which is a separate tool.

add.issue.name: Agents AGENTS.md: `dispatch coding` routes to a big-pickle-pool worker, and worker-mimo pins a model the console dropped

edit.description.md:
`/storage/Agents/AGENTS.md` contradicts itself on the one rule that exists to protect the main model's quota.

- `:139` — "The main model (big-pickle / nemotron-3-ultra-free) is the primary rate-limit bottleneck — **preserve it by offloading** non-trivial work to subagents."
- `:143` — "**Coding / implementation** → `worker-mimo` (console `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`). Strong coder; **use for coding by default**."
- `:173`, `:221`, `:247` repeat the `worker-mimo` routing (secretary pattern, programmer role, mechanic role).

`mimo` is **pool 1 — it shares big-pickle's quota** (topology in `/storage/Agents/.agents/shared-notes.md`, "Rate-limit pool topology (2026-09-27)"). So the default coding route spends the quota the line above it says to preserve, and it *is* the default: every dispatched coding task takes it.

**It is also self-refuting in practice.** `:141` tells agents to get the worker from `python3 $XLIB/tools/agent-coord.py dispatch <category>` — and that command's WORKER_MAP (`tools/agent-coord.py:540`) returns **`worker-north-mini-code`**. XLib's own AGENTS.md was already fixed this way (`8cb4daf`, plus the WORKER_MAP fix, both committed). The Agents file is the one left behind: `worker-mimo.md`'s description was already updated ("dispatch coding currently maps to worker-north-mini-code") and its parent doc was not.

**Second, mechanical defect — the pin is stale.** `worker-mimo.md` pins `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`. `opencode models` (verified 2026-09-27) no longer lists v2.5; it lists **`opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`**. A pin to a model the provider dropped is a dead worker behind a live name — the shared rule already says "ALWAYS verify with `opencode models` before pinning a model ID in an agent file".

**Fix, two parts:**

1. Re-point the four routing lines in `/storage/Agents/AGENTS.md` to `worker-north-mini-code` — or to whatever `9J30DNW` settles — so the doc matches the tool it tells agents to run, and coding stops defaulting into the protected pool.
2. Re-point `worker-mimo.md`'s `model:` to `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, or delete the agent if nothing routes to it any more. Do not leave a broken pin.

**Related, not duplicate.** `9J30DNW` decides *which model codes best* (mimo fails outright; nemotron-3-ultra vs north-mini-code on quality, with the shared OpenRouter `:free` pool as the cost tiebreak). This ticket is the rule-level contradiction plus a stale pin, and it does not need that comparison settled. If `9J30DNW` picks the worker, part 1 collapses to a one-line edit.

add.issue.name: worker-space-bunny agent — record only; needs a justified reasoning level before it goes near any agent file

edit.description.md:
**This is a record, not a build order.** The human has been testing Space Bunny for a few days and it was unavailable until recently — do not wire it into an agent yet.

`opencode/space-bunny-free` is worth a worker slot for two reasons:

- **Pool 2** — appears fully separate from big-pickle's quota; heavy concurrent use of both has never throttled either. Both pools are worth protecting.
- **The only console model reachable unauthenticated** through the Zen gateway: 7 of the 8 free console models return `403 "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode"`. Evidence in `plans/model-benchmark.md`; Cloudflare also rejects Python `urllib` at that gateway (error 1010) while curl passes, so probe with curl.

The human rates it co-equal with Big Pickle: *"Big Pickle and Space Bunny are special because they check themselves instead of making a guess and running with it."*

**Measured so far:** `library/ai/models/space-bunny.md` — the `invoicer` episode, 3 repeats, grade **`autonomy` ×3** (6–7 turns, 10–13k tokens), ~4× cheaper in tokens and ~10× faster than the model it beat, while grading higher. One episode is not a grade: this is a promising signal, not a licence.

**The open question — the human's to answer: what reasoning level?** They have been running the most expensive setting. That is not a defensible default unless it is *shown* to beat lower settings, so any worker file must carry a **justified** reasoning effort, not the max. `$XLIB/tools/modelbench/` is the harness that could settle it; note also that reasoning models need `--max-tokens ≳ 12288` in an agent loop or they return empty content wearing `finish_reason: length`.

**Current state:** `worker-space-bunny.md` does not exist in either workspace. Filed from the XLib board because this repo holds the only epiq project; the file it would create lives in `/storage/Agents/.opencode/agent/`.

add.issue.comment.md:
Cross-reference: `Q397WZG`. Verifying the routing while preparing it turned up a fact this ticket's cost analysis is missing, and it moves the deciding question.

**`mimo` shares big-pickle's quota.** It is pool 1, same as the main model — so keeping `worker-mimo` as the coding route spends the very quota the dispatch rule exists to protect, which is a different objection from the quality one this ticket weighs. `/storage/Agents/AGENTS.md:139` says to preserve big-pickle by offloading; `:143` then routes coding to a worker that offloads *into* that same pool, at 4 places (`:143`, `:173`, `:221`, `:247`).

Also: `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` is no longer listed by the console (verified with `opencode models` today; v2.5 gone, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free` present) — a second, independent reason the pin cannot stay, on top of the `UnknownError` recorded above.

Neither point changes *which model codes best*, which is what this ticket decides. But they do mean the status quo has no defence: if the comparison lands on `worker-north-mini-code` the pool problem is solved by the edit, and if it lands on `nemotron-3-ultra` it is solved because that model is a separate pool. There is no outcome of this comparison that leaves `worker-mimo` as the default.

add.issue.name: tasks.csv header declares 5 columns while every new row carries 8 — header-driven readers mis-map silently

edit.description.md:
Found while auditing taskview after the category/tag rollout (2026-09-27).

**The defect.** `~/.local/share/taskview/tasks.csv` carries the *old* header line:

    id,status,title,due_ts,chg_ts

but the schema is 8 columns (`// Schema:` comment line says so) and `ensure_csv` in `tools/taskview/taskupdate.py:20` writes 8 when it creates a file. It no-ops when the file already exists, so the on-disk header never self-heals. Field census of the live file: 63 rows with 5 fields, 48 with 8, 7 with 6, the rest wider (quoted titles containing commas — those parse fine).

**Why it matters.** `taskupdate.py` itself reads *positionally* (`row[5]`, guarded by `len(row) >`), so the tool is correct. The trap is any **header-driven** reader: `csv.DictReader` trusts that line and silently puts `category` under `due_ts` and shifts everything after. That already cost one session a whole table it was building for the human. A quiet wrong answer is worse than a crash.

**Fix options, pick one.**
- Repair the header on open (rewrite the field-name line, and migrate the 5-field rows to 8 so the file stops being mixed-format).
- Or drop the header line entirely and treat position 5-8 as optional — the readers already guard with `len(row) >`.
- Or leave the data alone and add a `taskupdate.py migrate` that reports the mixed format without writing.

**Definition of done.** A reader built on the header agrees with a positional reader for every id in the file, and there is a test that fails on the current file. Needs a spec line + tests per `XLib/doc/development.md` — taskview is committed (`250aaf1`), so this is real code, not scratch.

Related: the `tasks.csv` duplication between taskview and this board is `JM8GVW8`; vocabulary drift in the same file is `SNXBR23`.

add.issue.name: taskupdate.py: add `show <id>` — there is no lookup, so a task can only be found by reading the CSV

edit.description.md:
Found 2026-09-27, from the human: *"Referring to tasks by ID is convenient, but I don't have a quick reference right now."*

**The gap.** `taskupdate.py` has `add`, `update`, `done`, `cancel` — and **no lookup**. To answer "what is #40?" or "what is still open in `work`?" an agent has to open `~/.local/share/taskview/tasks.csv` and parse it by hand. The parsing is where `AQQNPAN` bites: hand-rolled readers get the columns wrong, silently.

**Proposed.** `taskupdate.py show <id>` printing the last row for that id as `id / status / title / due / category / tags / importance`, plus `--field <name>` for one value (an agent that wants just the category should not have to screen-scrape). `show` with no id, or `show --category work`, can list the open set — but keep that minimal; the *wide* multi-axis view is `E5MH4S2` and this must not grow into a second one.

Roughly five lines against the existing positional reader. Also worth taking in the same change: a `taskupdate.py list` that prints `id` first, so the CSV never has to be read raw.

**Definition of done.** `show` on a known id, on an unknown id (non-zero exit, clear message), and on an id whose rows are mixed-width (5-field and 8-field history) — all correct, with tests. Spec line + tests per `XLib/doc/development.md`.

This is the piece that makes `AQQNPAN` and the pane-id ticket (`#` rendering) worth having: ids are only useful as references if something can resolve them.

add.issue.name: taskview pane shows no task id — a task can only be named by its truncated title

edit.description.md:
Found 2026-09-27, from the human: *"Referring to tasks by ID is convenient, but I don't have a quick reference right now."*

**The gap.** The tmux task pane renders title only — `truncate(current['title'], width - 2)` at `tools/taskview/taskview.py:371` for the current task, `:389` for the UPCOMING list. No id appears anywhere, so the pane cannot answer "which one is this?" Two titles sharing a first few words are indistinguishable, and truncated titles are worse.

Concrete symptom from this session: asked whether `#40` was the task about part switching, the only handle available was the number — the title had been truncated out of recognition.

**Proposed.** Prefix the id in both places, `#<id> ` before the title, and widen the truncation budget by the prefix width so the title does not get shorter. Formatting lives in the render layer, so this is presentation, not data.

**Half of a pair — read with `EY72YA9`.** Showing an id creates references, and right now resolving one means reading the CSV by hand, which is the exact failure mode `AQQNPAN` describes. Land the lookup (`EY72YA9`) with this, not after: an id in the pane that nothing can resolve is a worse gap than no id at all. The id prefix is nearly free on its own; the pair is what removes the "no quick reference" problem.

add.issue.name: epiq state branch has never been pushed; agent events sit uncommitted and every cross-process sync is skipped

edit.description.md:
**The remote is not the problem — the sync path never runs.** Everything on this board exists on one machine only.

**Verified 2026-09-27:**

- epiq pushes the state branch to `origin` (hardcoded in the package), i.e. XLib's own remote `git@github.com:Xonok/XLib.git`. `git push --dry-run origin __epiq_state__` → `* [new branch] __epiq_state__ -> __epiq_state__`. Auth and write access are fine.
- `git ls-remote origin` lists **only** `refs/heads/master`. `__epiq_state__` has never been pushed. There is no remote copy of any ticket, comment or event in this project.
- Local state branch head is `cef330e`, dated **2026-09-26 21:08**. Nothing since has been committed.
- `epiq_sync` from an MCP session returns `skipped: true` every time (4 attempts today). `.epiq/log/epiq.log` has the reason once: `Skipping sync: the state worktree is held by sync (pid 1279 on Dreamer, started 2026-09-27T11:24:42.470Z)`. The TUI's autosync re-takes the lock on a ~10 s cycle, so a one-shot sync from another process loses the race.
- The log's only other message, thousands of times: `[sync] no own event file changes to commit`. **Sync commits only the calling actor's own event file.** The TUI (actor `xonok`) has nothing of its own to commit, so it never creates a commit — and a commit is the precondition for a push.

**Live consequence.** `Q397WZG`, `DY56JS1` and the `9J30DNW` comment exist **only** in `.epiq/events/g3eadtng57jjeep7b2c7fasva7~pending.jsonl` (22 KB, mtime 14:43) inside the state worktree at `/home/xonok/.epiq-global/worktrees/01M3BVECGNWADVFNJ4311DGPGH/`. Uncommitted, unpushed. If that worktree is pruned or reinstalled, they are gone.

**Options (all need the human — a push is a git change, and the lock holder is their TUI):**

1. Quit the epiq TUI (pid 1279) so nothing competes for the lock, then run one sync from an MCP session. The first real commit also triggers the first push (`-u origin __epiq_state__`), fixing the missing remote in the same action. Not verified from here: I will not kill the human's live TUI.
2. `:sync` inside the TUI does **not** work around this — per the mechanism above it only commits `xonok`'s own event file.
3. Longer term this is a design hole worth reporting upstream: a per-actor commit rule means any actor that never syncs itself silently loses its writes. A "commit all pending event files" path, or a documented `own`-actor override, would remove the failure mode.

Three `epiq-mcp` processes are alive alongside the TUI (4h48m, 18h13m and ~5m old), so lock contention has more than one possible source.

add.issue.name: xlint: flag absolute system paths in tracked Markdown — a tracked file that syncs between machines must not name one machine's layout

edit.description.md:
Raised by the human 2026-09-27 after a path sweep of the Agents workspace: *"As always, tracked files should not contain full system paths."* The rule had no written home and no mechanical check, so it kept slipping — 20 occurrences across 6 tracked files before this was cleaned by hand.

**Why it matters, twice over.** A tracked file is versioned *and* synced between machines, so an absolute path is wrong in the ordinary way (it means nothing on Dreamer, gab, Xena or the LXC) and in the git way (it records one machine's layout as if it were the project's). The designated home already exists: `.agents/machine-info.md` is git-ignored *precisely* so it can hold machine-specific facts. That makes this a layering rule with a known landing place, not a matter of taste.

**Proposed check.** In the `.md` branch, flag a path-like token that starts with `/storage/`, `/home/<user>/`, `/root/`, or `~/`. Message should name the file, the line, and the landing place: *point at `.agents/machine-info.md`, or make the path repo-relative.*

**Exemptions to design for, each with a reason** — a naive check would fire on all of these:

- `.agents/machine-info.md` itself, and anything git-ignored. It is the destination, not a violation. Detection has to be "is this file tracked", not "is it a `.md`".
- `AGENTS.md` setup walkthrough — `ln -s /path/to/XLib/tools …` and an `scp -r /storage/Agents/ …` example. The machine path is the *content* there.
- Plans that describe **another** machine's layout. `plans/remote-opencode-lxc.md` is six `/root/...` paths on the LXC host, and naming them is the document's subject.
- Paths quoted as **evidence**. A model-benchmark row quotes `/home/user/project/relative/path.py` — a fictional path a model copied verbatim, cited as proof of harness defect E9. It describes no real location.

That last pair is the honest hard part: the check cannot be "contains a slash-heavy token", it has to be a deliberate judgement about whether the path is *about* something or *about where something is*. Worth writing the exemptions into the spec rather than discovering them as false positives later.

**Process.** An xlint rule gets a plan doc under `XLib/doc/plans/` and tests, like the frontmatter/fence rule — see `GBNEWPS` for the shape and `XLib/doc/plans/xlint-frontmatter-fence-skip.md`. Same file and same one-deep `.md` branch as `GBNEWPS` and `PMRBFR3`; all three should be implemented together or at least not conflict.

Suggested spec line for the rule itself, if the human wants the convention written down as well as enforced — one line in `AGENTS.md`: *tracked files name paths relative to a repo, or point at `.agents/machine-info.md` for machine locations.* The check catches the symptom; the line explains it to the agent that writes the next file.

add.issue.comment.md: Third rule for the same one-deep `.md` branch — filed as `7HP67R2` (flag absolute system paths in tracked Markdown). Recording the overlap here so whoever implements one of them knows the others exist: `GBNEWPS` and `PMRBFR3` both change the `.md` branch's line-scanning, and `7HP67R2` adds a per-line token check on top. All three touch `xlint/xlint.py` in the same function, so they want one implementation session or a deliberate order, not three parallel ones.

add.issue.comment.md:
**A second, distinct fence bug found while converting notes to tabs (2026-09-27) — indented fences are not recognised at all.** In `xlint/xlint.py` `_fence_exempt`, the `line[0].isspace()` branch runs *before* the fence-character test and `continue`s without setting `in_fence`. So a code fence nested inside a list item (the normal way to write one — ```` ```sh ```` indented under a `- ` or `1. ` item) never opens fence state, its contents are treated as ordinary Markdown, and every space-indented line inside it is flagged. The closing fence is indented too, so state never recovers either.

Consequence worth stating plainly: for such a file **lint-clean is unachievable without editing the inside of a code block** — you either convert code-block content to tabs, or leave the violations. That is the choice I had to make in `agent-notes-a4.md`, where a ```` ```sh ```` COSMIC install block sits inside an ordered list item; I converted its continuation lines to tabs (shell continuation lines under `| \`, so nothing functional changed) and would rather the linter had exempted them.

The fix is the same shape as this ticket's, just applied after stripping the indent: test `line.lstrip()` for the fence characters rather than `line[0]`. Worth covering both cases in one implementation — a fence at column 0 and a fence nested in a list — plus a test with an indented fence whose body is space-indented, which fails today.

add.issue.name: oc-agent: stop allocating its own agent number — take the name from agent-coord and render it everywhere (title, ports, env, board identity)

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Agent names come from two independent allocators, so the name the human sees can disagree with the name the agent works under. `oc-agent` picks its own instance number by `mkdir` probing `/tmp/oc-agent/$AGENT/$AGENT.$N` (lines 9–21) and uses it for the terminal title and the port file; `agent-coord.py` allocates `workspace/role-N` separately in `ids.json`, keyed by pid, recycled by `recycle_dead_slots`. Nothing ties the two together — the tab can say `secretary-3` while the notes file is `agent-notes-secretary-5.md`. The human hit exactly that mismatch on 2026-09-29.

**The human's direction (2026-09-29):** "We already have a mechanism for giving names to agents, the same mechanism should be used for as many things as is reasonable." The mechanism is agent-coord (`workspace/role-N` via `OPENCODE_AGENT_ROLE`). oc-agent must consume that name, not mint its own, and it should be rendered everywhere from one source:

1. **Move `~/.local/bin/oc-agent` (machine-local, untracked, 79 lines of bash) into `tools/oc-agent`** — the human's ruling: anything relating to oc-agent is XLib work. Tracked, so every machine gets the same allocator and the same title/port/env behavior.
2. **oc-agent takes its identity from agent-coord** (`coord id`) instead of allocating `$N` itself: same `role`, same `N`, same workspace for (a) the terminal title (lines 24–25), (b) the port-file `role` field (line 59), (c) `OPENCODE_AGENT_ROLE` (line 27 — feeds `ctx` and agent-coord).
3. **The board identity derives from the same role, not from a manual `/rename`.** epiq identities are `opencode/<role>` (e.g. `opencode/secretary`); an agent announces that name and the window already carries it because oc-agent set the title from the same role at launch. No `/rename` prompt should ever be needed.
4. Keep the `~/.opencode/ports/*.json` behavior — watchers (skynet etc.) read it. `OPENCODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` stays so opencode doesn't overwrite the title.

**Open question for the human when implementing:** precedence — agent-coord already honours an `OPENCODE_AGENT_ID` override; confirm the allocator lives in agent-coord and oc-agent only renders (per the human's framing, yes).

**Related:** notes side of the same split is its own ticket (notes ref). Don't break an agent started without oc-agent: it must still get the same allocator, it just cannot set the title (no tty).

add.issue.name: Agent notes: bind the note file to the canonical id at session start, and make look-through → promote → clear the enforced protocol

edit.description.md:
**Problem.** Two failures the human named on 2026-09-29:

1. **The note file is claimed unreliably.** Nothing creates or locks the *instance* note file at session start; `coord instance-note` only prints a path derived from the id. Instance numbers come from two independent allocators (agent-coord's `ids.json` vs oc-agent's own), so the number shown in the tab and the number in the notes file an agent actually writes can disagree (see the oc-agent ticket for that side).
2. **Instance notes become biographies.** The intended lifecycle — look through the instance notes, persist what is important, then clear the file — is only a convention in `doc/plans/agent-coord-role-notes.md` ("Discarded on /new unless agent promotes"), so files grow unbounded and the next session inherits every past session's context. The human's ruling: at the **start of every session**, look through the instance note file, persist the important things (promote to `role-notes-<role>.md` / `shared-notes.md` / `HISTORY.md`), then **clear the file** — instance notes stay focused on the current task.

**Scoped work (implementer to refine with the human):**

1. Fix the allocator so the note filename always matches the id the window shows — one source of truth (the oc-agent ticket ships that).
2. Mechanize the session-start protocol instead of relying on convention: a `coord` entry point that stamps a session header on the instance note at start, and makes the previous session's look-through+clear a visible, required step — e.g. the command exits nonzero with a reminder until the stale content is promoted and the file cleared. **No silent truncation**: clearing must be the agent's explicit, after-reading act; the tool can require it, it must not do it.
3. Make promotion cheap: `coord role-claim role-notes-<role>` already exists; a one-shot "promote my instance notes into the role notes" helper turns the look-through into a command.
4. Update `AGENTS.md` (both workspaces): "read your notes before starting later sessions" becomes the concrete look-through → promote → clear protocol above.
5. Refresh `doc/plans/agent-coord-role-notes.md`: it still documents the dead `a1..a8` slot format and predates the role-N implementation; its lifecycle section must state the human's start-of-session ruling.

**Related:** the timestamped human-conversation log (R87HJJN) is a different deliverable but shares this notes-discipline thread.

add.issue.name: xcsv: the tokenizer lost its `peek` lookahead helper in a review pass — restore it or rule it out on purpose

edit.description.md:
What happened, already checked:

- `peek(c)` was a local closure in the Python tokenizer — `i + 1 < line_len and line[i + 1] == c`. Added in `fd05cb9` (2026-09-07, "Rename some things to avoid conflict with python inbuilts").
- Inlined away at both call sites in `f0b81d0` (2026-09-10, "Updated xcsv and had it reviewed many times").
- The tokenizer then moved out of `xcsv.py` into `dev/xcsv/_/csv_tok.py` (plain Python, despite the `_` naming). The inlined condition survives at `dev/xcsv/_/csv_tok.py:27` — the escaped-quote case. The other call site was the comment check, which is now a `startswith("//")` test at the top of the line.
- Nothing named `peek` is left in xcsv. The only `peek` in the repo is `agent-coord.py --peek`, an unrelated flag.

What is open:

- Was dropping it right? `doc/style/common.md` names this exact pattern and says to factor it into `peek_char()` — so the tokenizer was following the house rule when the review pass removed the helper.
- Decide deliberately: restore a named lookahead, or rule it out and say why. The module is 56 lines, so either is cheap.
- Also worth a look while in there: the other repeated conditions in the same function (`i < line_len and line[i] == ","` appears three times) are the case the style rule describes.

add.issue.name: Process rules: make AI simplify code on its own — needs intent from the human before it is actionable

edit.description.md:
Wanted: a standing rule so an agent **simplifies the code it writes or touches** without being asked, instead of simplification only happening when the human asks for it.

**Blocked on intent the human has to supply.** Tagged `human-input-needed`; not actionable until he provides it, because "simplify" with no boundary is a regression generator rather than an improvement.

What he needs to decide:

- What counts as simplified — shorter, fewer branches, no premature abstraction? And what must be left exactly as it is.
- When an agent may **not** simplify: working code it did not write, code with no tests, anything mid-migration (Traveller is mid-migration right now).
- Whether simplification needs a sign-off, or is allowed silently with a note.

Evidence of the failure mode this rule has to tell apart — already in the repo, see the xcsv `peek` ticket: a review-heavy pass inlined a named one-character lookahead away in the tokenizer (`f0b81d0`, 2026-09-10). Fewer lines, less legible, and against the letter of `doc/style/common.md`, which names that exact pattern and says to factor it into `peek_char()`. That is what an over-eager simplification looks like when nothing says where the line is.

Where the answer belongs: the intent rules, not this ticket. `personal/<person>/intent.md` in the Agents workspace is the generic home for them (see the Intent section of `AGENTS.md`); a large task's own intent is task-specific.
